session.question: In the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, which multi-criteria decision analysis methods were compared, and what did the sensitivity analysis reveal about their suitability and differences in calculation and interpretation?
session.answer:
The study compared five multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems: weighted sum method (WSM), TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA (Data Envelopment Analysis). It applied these methods to 12 district heating companies using 8 criteria. (daugavietis2022acomparisonof chunk 1)

The sensitivity analysis examined how robust the rankings were under several weight-adjustment schemes, including individual criterion changes, fixed-value weight changes, and a comparison between analytic hierarchy process (AHP)-derived weights and equal weights. It showed that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analysis of district heating systems, but they are not interchangeable: they differ in calculation procedure and in how their outcomes are interpreted. The paper therefore concluded that method choice should be guided by the intended decision context and interpretation needs. It also proposed a generalized algorithm for future energy-system sustainability assessments. (daugavietis2022acomparisonof chunk 1)

pqac-015cdb1b: The paper compared five multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems: WSM, TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA. It evaluated 12 district heating companies using 8 criteria. Sensitivity analysis varied criteria weights in several ways, including individual changes, fixed-value changes, and AHP versus equal weights. The results, together with literature review, showed that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analyses of district heating systems, but they differ in their calculation procedures and in how their results are interpreted. The study also proposed a generalized algorithm to guide future energy-system sustainability assessments.
From Jānis Daugavietis, Raimonda Soloha, Elīna Dāce, and Jeļena Ziemele. A comparison of multi-criteria decision analysis methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems. Energies, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/en15072411, doi:10.3390/en15072411.

pqac-0aba586f: The paper compares five multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems: WSM, TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA. It evaluates 12 district heating companies using 8 criteria. A sensitivity analysis is used to judge method credibility by changing criterion weights in several ways: testing stability ranges of alternatives, changing weights by a fixed value, and comparing AHP-derived weights with equal weights. The study concludes that all methods are suitable for district heating sustainability analysis, but they differ in calculation procedures and result interpretation. It also provides a generalized algorithm for energy-sector sustainability assessment.
From Jānis Daugavietis, Raimonda Soloha, Elīna Dāce, and Jeļena Ziemele. A comparison of multi-criteria decision analysis methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems. Energies, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/en15072411, doi:10.3390/en15072411.

pqac-ad173e98: The excerpt describes a 2023 study on sustainable supplier evaluation using multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods in a fuzzy environment. The authors evaluated battery suppliers with ARAS, EDAS, MAIRCA, TOPSIS, and VIKOR and performed sensitivity analysis. They found the methods produced similar rankings, supported by WS similarity measure and weighted Spearman correlation. The sensitivity analysis suggested the most important criteria were transportation cost, delivery time, and warranty period. This is relevant to questions about MCDA method comparison, sensitivity analysis, and interpretation of criteria importance in sustainability assessment.
From Jakub Więckowski, Bartłomiej Kizielewicz, Andrii Shekhovtsov, and Wojciech Sałabun. How do the criteria affect sustainable supplier evaluation? - a case study using multi-criteria decision analysis methods in a fuzzy environment. Journal of Engineering Management and Systems Engineering, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.56578/jemse020102, doi:10.56578/jemse020102.

pqac-960f0a01: The paper evaluates solar district heating systems (SDHS) for nearly zero energy and positive energy buildings using a sustainability analysis across technical, economic, environmental, and social dimensions. It proposes a machine-learning-based decision-support framework combining multi-objective optimization and multi-criteria decision making (MCDA) to create a sustainability index for stakeholders and policymakers. The case study compares retrofitted residential communities of different sizes in Emmen (Netherlands) against a decentralized heat pump. Results show up to 95% solar fraction, economic feasibility for NZEB only from 100 houses onward, and environmental/social improvements versus the heat pump. The excerpt does not mention specific MCDA method comparisons, sensitivity analysis details, or calculation interpretation.
From Mohamed Hany Abokersh, Sachin Gangwar, Marleen Spiekman, Manel Vallès, Laureano Jiménez, and Dieter Boer. Sustainability insights on emerging solar district heating technologies to boost the nearly zero energy building concept. Renewable Energy, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2021.08.091, doi:10.1016/j.renene.2021.08.091.

pqac-85efbcde: The paper compares multiple Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) methods and normalization techniques for holistic sustainability assessment in engineering, using an aviation case study. Sustainability is treated as a trade-off among five dimensions: performance, environmental, economic, social, and circularity, aggregated into a Sustainability Index (SI). The study also tests sensitivity to initial data and weight variations. Results show that most MCDM/normalization combinations produce similar rankings of alternatives, but the weighted sum method with min-max normalization was judged most suitable in this use case because it is robust to small data changes while remaining sensitive to larger ones. The work stresses careful method selection for transparent, reliable assessments.
From Sonia Malefaki, Dionysios Markatos, Angelos Filippatos, and Spiros Pantelakis. A comparative analysis of multi-criteria decision-making methods and normalization techniques in holistic sustainability assessment for engineering applications. Aerospace, 2025. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/aerospace12020100, doi:10.3390/aerospace12020100.

contexts.context: The excerpt describes a 2021 Applied Energy paper that develops an integrated sustainability assessment model using hybrid multi-criteria decision making (MCDA) methods. It combines four fuzzy MCDA techniques: Fuzzy SWARA, Fuzzy MOORA, Fuzzy WASPAS, and Fuzzy TOPSIS to assess social, economic, environmental, and technical factors and to validate results across methods. session.formatted_answer:
Question: In the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, which multi-criteria decision analysis methods were compared, and what did the sensitivity analysis reveal about their suitability and differences in calculation and interpretation?

The study compared five multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods for sustainability assessment of district heating systems: weighted sum method (WSM), TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA (Data Envelopment Analysis). It applied these methods to 12 district heating companies using 8 criteria. (daugavietis2022acomparisonof chunk 1)

The sensitivity analysis examined how robust the rankings were under several weight-adjustment schemes, including individual criterion changes, fixed-value weight changes, and a comparison between analytic hierarchy process (AHP)-derived weights and equal weights. It showed that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analysis of district heating systems, but they are not interchangeable: they differ in calculation procedure and in how their outcomes are interpreted. The paper therefore concluded that method choice should be guided by the intended decision context and interpretation needs. It also proposed a generalized algorithm for future energy-system sustainability assessments. (daugavietis2022acomparisonof chunk 1)
